previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Factor V Leiden and a known ascending aortic thrombus was admitted for recurrent pleuritic chest pain. Imaging showed the aortic thrombus was unchanged from a prior scan three weeks earlier, with no evidence of pulmonary embolism or acute cardiac ischemia. The chest pain was determined to be non-anginal and likely musculoskeletal, exacerbated by persistent coughing. The patient expressed frustration with chronic pain and Lovenox injections but declined warfarin therapy. Anticoagulation was continued, and gabapentin and tizanidine were restarted. A cough suppressant was added to alleviate symptoms. The patient was discharged home with instructions to continue Lovenox, follow up with vascular surgery, and monitor for changes in symptoms.
problems: Embolism and thrombosis of thoracic aorta

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o male with Factor V Leiden deficiency on Lovenox for 
recurrent deep vein thromboses and pulmonary emboli, most 
recently with an ascending aortic thrombus who presented with 
recurrent pleuritic chest pain consistent with musculoskeletal 
etiology and abdominal pain of unknown etiology.
.
1. Chest Pain: He has had multiple hospitalizations with 
recurrent pleuritic chest pain with several in the weeks 
preceding this admission. CTA, CXR and EKG were unconcerning for 
new embolic events. Cardiac enzymes were negative times three. A 
musculoskeletal pain from persistent coughing and 
bronchotracheal irritation were considered most likely origins 
of his chest pain. Patient was maintained on outpatient narcotic 
contract per discussions with his primary care physician. Social 
work saw as inpatient to advise with coping strategies and 
assist with outpatient resources for pain management. Patient 
refused to see a pain specialist. Patient reported that he had 
not been taking his Gabapentin, Tizanidine or Venlafaxine. He 
was discharged without refills for his narcotics but with close 
follow-up appointments. 
.
2. Abdominal Pain: Patient reported chronic problems with 
abdominal pain after several abdominal surgeries. Patient also 
reported pain at his sites of Lovenox injection. Abdominal CT 
did not reveal obstruction. Patient reported normal bowel habits 
with no complaints of constipation. Pain was likely due to 
multiple abdominal surgeries and chronic abdominal injections. 
No further evaluation was performed as an inpatient. 
.
3. Factor V Leiden/Recurrent Thrombotic/Embolic Events: No new 
thromboses or emboli were detected on US or CT. Patient recently 
had infrarenal IVC filter placed at another hospital. Patient 
was maintained on Lovenox (Enoxaparin) throughout his admission.
.
4. Elevated WBC Count: Patient was discharged from another 
hospital the day of admission to ___. He had been treated with 
steroids for a possible asthma exacerbation. His elevated white 
count with left shift was attributed to the steroids and not 
infection. 
.
5. Depression/chronic pain: Patient struggles with his multiple 
diagnoses and anxiety seems to be impairing his ability to 
function. Patient has not been taking Neurontin, Venlafaxine or 
Tizanidine as prescribed. Taking Clonazepam for anxiety. Social 
work saw as inpatient. Had psychiatry follow-up as an 
outpatient. 
.
6. Hyperlipidemia: Stable. Continued outpatient Simvastatin.
.
7. Cough: Patient reports chronic cough with occasional 
hemoptysis after multiple interventional pulmonary procedures. 
Continued home Albuterol and Advair. Received 
Guaifenesin-Dextromethorphan as needed for cough.
.
8. Hypertension: Normotensive throughout stay. Continued on 
home-dose of HCTZ and Amlodipine.
